topology.partition_note: One parquet table per split. The population is a flat set of light curves rather than a set of files, so a run selects a FRACTION of stars inside the single partition instead of naming partitions; the data path refuses target_partitions and subset_ref for that reason.
topology.sample_unit: one TESS light curve (one star observed in one sector)
topology.identity_note: (GaiaID, sector) is unique in every released split. (TIC, sector) is NOT unique in train and must never be keyed on.
topology.grouping_note: Splits are grouped by Gaia DR3 identifier: no star appears in two splits. Sub-portion draws inside a split are taken over STARS for the same reason.
topology.population_note: test is the held-out final-evaluation population. It is not described here beyond its size, carries no row or target in the committed manifest, and is never staged into a run's data directory.

preprocessing.length_rule: right-truncate to 1024, or pad with the last observed flux value
preprocessing.normalization: per-light-curve z-score of the observed samples, applied BEFORE padding

topology.native_length_note: Released curves run 542..3917 samples (median 1124), bimodal: the ~1.0-1.2k cluster is the 30-minute-cadence Primary Mission and the ~3.5-3.9k cluster is the 10-minute-cadence first Extended Mission. The frozen 1024 window therefore truncates most Extended-Mission curves; it is PhyTS appendix D.2 parity, not an optimum.
